title: DC-area forecast: More heat and humidity today, plus late-day strong storms possible
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Highs mainly in the upper 80s and low 90s this afternoon – humidity makes it feel 10 degrees hotter. Partial sun ahead of storms probably popping midafternoon into evening. A few could be strong.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Highs mainly in the upper 80s and low 90s this afternoon – humidity makes it feel 10 degrees hotter. Partial sun ahead of storms probably popping midafternoon into evening. A few could be strong to severe, with a severe thunderstorm watch for most of the region until 9 p.m.

What’s next? More upper 80s to mid-90s this weekend. Humidity may ease slightly over time, but barely noticeable if so. Late-day storm chances are common, although strong storm chances could wane beyond Saturday.

Today’s daily digit — 3/10:  The hottest and most humid spots may feel like low 100s this afternoon. Scattered strong afternoon storms are also possible. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Friday): Partly sunny skies. Humidity remains high, with dew points around the low 70s making it feel as hot as the upper 90s to low 100s. Actual highs are again mainly upper 80s to low 90s, but some mid-90s are possible. Some showers and storms probably start to move into the region from the west after 3 or 4 p.m. A few could be strong during the late afternoon into early evening, with potential for damaging winds in addition to heavy rain. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: The heaviest of any downpours and gusty storms try to exit the region to the east by about 8 or 9 p.m. Humid lows barely dip near 70 to the mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Saturday): Partly sunny again. Sultry highs range from the upper 80s to mid-90s as it stays humid (dew points near 70 to the low 70s). Once again, late afternoon to early evening is the most likely timing for some scattered storms, a few with flooding downpours and damaging wind gusts possible. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Evening storms remain probable but intensity tapers again after 8 or 9 p.m. Sticky lows near 70 to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Sunday: Storm chances appear to be lower as it appears now, but a couple could still bubble up late in the day. Skies are mostly sunny. Comparatively tolerable humidity? Dew points near or below 70 are still high enough to make highs within a few degrees of 90 rather uncomfortable. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

Sunday night: A bit more humid after any pop-up shower or storm during the evening. Lows only dip again near 70 to mid-70s. Skies are partly to mostly clear. Confidence: Medium

Hot highs in the low to mid-90s are likely Monday and Tuesday. A slight chance for late afternoon and evening storms popping up as a cold front approaches and eventually passes. The front offers only a bit of humidity relief later Monday into midweek. Confidence: Medium

Shower and storm chances may continue into a slightly less-warm midweek.

DC weather history for August 7

A violent 2000 thunderstorm turned deadly when a lightning strike killed a man near the West Falls Church Metro, as the storm brought widespread damage and downed trees across the region.
